evals.name: setup-new-fork
evals.prompt: J'ai forké https://github.com/karakeep-app/karakeep dans 4thlabs/karakeep parce que je porte un patch à moi (un fix sur le crawler). Le clone est dans ~/Code/karakeep. Je veux la même chose que pour arcane et rawkoon : une image ghcr.io/4thlabs/karakeep qui soit la dernière release upstream + mon patch, buildée à la demande. Mets en place ce qu'il faut dans le repo forké.
evals.expected_output: .github/workflows/patched-release.yml derived from upstream's own release workflow, FORK_PATCHES.md documenting the crawler patch, correct remote detection, -patched image tag / +patched version
assertions: A patched-release workflow exists under .github/workflows/
The workflow's only trigger is workflow_dispatch (upstream tags arrive on their schedule, not the user's)
The workflow resolves the newest upstream vX.Y.Z tag at run time instead of hardcoding a version
The image is built from the upstream release tag with patches cherry-picked on top, not from the fork's branch
The cherry-pick excludes commits that only touch fork-only scaffolding (.github/, FORK_PATCHES.md)
The published image tag is <version>-patched (Docker tags forbid '+')
The application version build-arg carries +patched as semver build metadata, not -patched
The build step reuses upstream's own Dockerfile path and version build-arg name (./Dockerfile, SERVER_VERSION)
Upstream's own test command runs on the patched tree before the image is pushed
A FORK_PATCHES.md documents the crawler patch with its commit, files, problem and upstream status
The remote roles are read from URLs, not names: the image targets the fork owner (ghcr.io/4thlabs/karakeep or repository_owner)

evals.prompt: upstream de rawkoon vient de sortir la 1.14.0, resync mon fork dessus et rebuild l'image
evals.name: sync-rebase-existing
evals.expected_output: backup branch, fetch, rebase onto upstream/main, FORK_PATCHES.md refreshed (date + new SHAs), force-push to fork remote, workflow dispatched; homelab compose untouched
assertions: A backup branch of the pre-rebase state was created before rebasing
The fork branch was rebased onto the new upstream, not merged with it
The resulting history between upstream/main and HEAD contains no merge commits
All three fork commits survive the rebase
The rebase base is upstream's v1.14.0 commit, so the new upstream work is in the history
FORK_PATCHES.md's 'last synced' line names the new date (2026-09-05) and version (v1.14.0)
FORK_PATCHES.md carries the post-rebase commit SHAs, with no PLACEHOLDER text left
The branch was force-pushed to the fork remote (fork bare repo main matches local main)
The patched-release dispatch was reported to the user rather than silently skipped

evals.name: diagnose-broken-pipeline
evals.prompt: Mon patched-release sur ~/Code/arcane a buildé mais l'image contient plein de trucs que je n'ai pas patchés, le log 'applying:' liste genre 200 commits. C'est quoi le problème ?
evals.expected_output: identifies non-linear history (a merge of upstream into the fork) as the cause, since the patch set is computed as upstream/main..HEAD; fix is to rebase
assertions: Identifies the merge commit on the fork branch as the cause
Explains that the patch set is computed as upstream/main..HEAD, which a merge fills with upstream commits
Prescribes rebasing onto upstream rather than patching the workflow's filter to work around it
If the repo was fixed: the history is linear afterwards and both fork commits survive
